title: Alone Together - Episode 3 - Games, Game Design, and World Building Mechanisms
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_9BI3P-OH84

Daniel (@dungeondive) and Allan of Perplexing Ruins open 2023 with an episode that drifts, productively, from haul to design theory. Early on Daniel addresses the *League of Dungeoneers* review discourse directly: five hours of coverage, fifteen minutes of honest criticism about inconsistently updated rules, and the internet fixated on the fifteen minutes.

The middle section is a shared reckoning with consumption. Zine Quest has grown past the point either can track; Allan admits a PDF library he hasn't read, and asks whether buying a game you never play is meaningful support at all. From this comes the episode's best idea — the **tail**. Games used to have long lives: Runebound and Arkham Horror were supported for years, so communities formed. Kickstarter delivers everything at once and the conversation dies on fulfilment. Allan's counter-model is Leo of *Vaults of Vaarn*, who grew a world across three zines, a blog, and a consolidated fourth volume — and that keeping *Fallen* alive is his actual roadmap.

They close on Daniel's own design, *Hall of Heroes*, where retiring characters unlock bonuses for successors, and Allan spitballs a tiered adventure-site structure on the spot.

----

Do you prefer games that arrive complete, or ones that grow a long tail over years?
